Krasnohrad New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Krasnohrad — known as Konstantinograd until 1922 — already had about 150 Jews when the town received city status in 1798, and its oldest communal ledger (pinkas) dates to 1810. About 90 Jews from Krasnohrad were murdered by the Nazis near the village of Natalyne in June 1942. This cemetery was gradually repurposed as a Christian graveyard through the second half of the 20th century; only two Jewish tombstones, dated 1947 and 1982, remain today.
